I watched Iron Lung today and I went in truly blind to the movie plot, never heard of the game, or even knew who Markiplier was. I was insanely impressed. I looked up reviews on YouTube to see what other people thought as this movie was stuck in my head for hours after I watched it and now I am a huge fan. I haven’t felt that level of emotion since I watched Interstellar. I’m a mom and my son said he wanted to watch it so we went to my small local cinema in Idaho and I was confused because others in the theater stayed through the credits. I figured extra credit scene? Now I’m watching this video and seeing how much happiness this is bringing him after soo much time and hard work he put into this project that I’m getting emotional all over again. All I can say now is I hope he gets to create more movies and I’m excited to see what he will create next and happy I can support the independent creators🍿♥️

I have sound and photo sensitive epilepsy. This movie was the first time I have been to a theater since I was 8 years old. I worked for weeks to make sure I would be able to see it safely. Meds, headphones, earplugs if i needed them, a blanket, my loving wife beside me, and over a year of nervous system regulation therapy. 

I watched the movie. It was the best movie I have ever seen. Genuinely. I didn't know what theaters were like. The way the floor shook with the base, how massive the screen was. The sound the lights it was all so intense. 

This movie was such a massive accomplishment, for mark, for the community, for indi film making. For me, it was proof that if I took care of myself, accomidated myself, I could do things again. I could leave my house. Be in a loud theater watching a horror movie with every seizure trigger under the sun blaring at me. 

I didn't seize. I was safe the whole movie. It was so intense. It felt like living for the first time in a long time. And I know a massive part of it was having this symbol of safety that has been carved into me since childhood standing at the helm, living through every bloody moment in this immersive masterpiece with me. 

I am getting better. And doing things. And living again. And I got to watch Iron Lung. Isn't that cool?
